clue.text: Eager to grasp essence of big picture

indicators.note: to grasp means the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: someone eager for something is panting for it

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, here its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone keen to take in the overall view of a situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big picture' reads as one phrase, but 'big' only supplies its middle letter I and 'picture' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a picture made with brush and pigment, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Safe bet Queen's found in Court

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A gambler's tip that the Queen will be present at court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link before the containment indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A cert, short for certainty, is informal British slang for a bet that cannot lose.

clue.text: Flower parts ultimately put in rings

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the bell sounds

parts.note: peals are rings of church bells

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word put

explanation.surface: An instruction to place the last bits of a flower into circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' suggests circles, but here it is the sound of bells, PEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Petals are the coloured leaves that make up a bloom's corolla.

clue.text: Check choke and accelerator

definitions.meaning: to check is to restrain or hold back, as in throttling back output
to choke someone is to strangle them by the neck
the pedal or lever controlling fuel flow to an engine

explanation.surface: A list of the controls on an old car or motorcycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: two verbs and a noun, all one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to suppress, to strangle, and the engine's speed control valve.

clue.text: New product from pub? Cheers!

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a round of cheers and applause

explanation.surface: A brewery launches something new and toasts it at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' looks like a toast but is applause.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is a novel invention or product brought to market.

clue.text: Chance men take to some degree, giving stick

indicators.note: to some degree says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gamblers' risks, measured, are what give them a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To cement is to bind or fix things firmly, the verb sense of glue together.

clue.text: Anonymous salesmen behaving improperly

indicators.note: letters behaving improperly are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Unidentified sales staff have been misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anonymous has no name given, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wise man keeps sober. That's me!

indicators.note: keeps means holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a seer is a wise prophet
TT, teetotal, means not drinking

explanation.surface: A sage stays off the drink, and the speaker claims to be him.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler speaks: 'me' is the person who wrote the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a crossword is called its setter, so the clue writer says this of themself.

clue.text: Turned in something educational

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A student hands in a piece of schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned in' reads as handed over, but 'in' is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hinged swung or pivoted about a joint, as a door does when it is turned.

clue.text: Outfit includes new tie

indicators.note: includes means the outfit holds the other letter

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit

explanation.surface: A set of clothes comes with a fresh necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join or bind together, as bones knit.

clue.text: Moon's rather complicated, not hard for this person

indicators.note: complicated letters are tangled into a new order
not says that letter is left out of the fodder

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone who studies the Moon complains that it is rather complex.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from MOONSRATHER leaves letters that rearrange to the answer; the definition refers back to the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the moon and other celestial bodies would find it complicated.

clue.text: Reportedly, underground workers could be little ones

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word spoken aloud gives one spelt otherwise

parts.note: miners work underground in pits

explanation.surface: Coal workers turn out to be children, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Minors are children under the legal age of adulthood.

clue.text: Old friend purchases outfit, fashionable at first

indicators.note: purchases means takes hold of, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: an ally is a friend
a rig is a set of clothes or gear
in means trendy

explanation.surface: A former friend buys some clothes that were trendy initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchases' means grips, the old sense of purchase as a hold: RIGIN sits between O and ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means in the beginning, synonymous with initially.

clue.text: New arrivals giving screams on hospital wing?

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts this piece after the other

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
rants are loud tirades

explanation.surface: Newly admitted patients are shrieking in a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrants are people coming in for the first time, newcomers.

clue.text: It's surrounded by blood, swelling

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first piece inside the other

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: A lump encircled by blood, as in a gory medical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland showing as a lump in the neck.

clue.text: 'About a Boy', occasionally read and debated

parts.note: re means concerning
a son is a boy

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of read

explanation.surface: Nick Hornby's novel About a Boy is studied and discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: About a Boy is a Nick Hornby novel and film, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reasoned is to have argued logically, like debating a matter.

clue.text: The man's upset, in trouble revealing bottom

indicators.note: in places the turned pronoun inside the other word

parts.note: a bind is an awkward predicament

indicators.note: upset in a down-reading sense means turned over, so the word is backwards

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A distressed man in difficulty accidentally exposes his rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind is a colloquial word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Design's altered comprising last of designer clothing

indicators.note: comprising means the shuffled letters hold the other one inside
altered says the letters are changed in order
last of takes the final letter of designer

explanation.surface: A fashion design is changed, including the final touch from its designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' makes DESSING from DESIGNS, and R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is the act of putting on clothes, so clothing in its verbal sense.

clue.text: Sheep low endlessly around Ireland?

indicators.note: around puts the shortened word outside the other
endlessly means the word for lowing loses its final letter

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound of cattle
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A sheep gives a stifled bleat across the Irish countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a breed of sheep prized for fine wool.

clue.text: Rule present covering this compiler's back

indicators.note: covering means the gift word goes round the other

parts.note: to present is to give or donate

indicators.note: back says those letters are written in reverse

parts.note: this compiler is, from the setter, I'm

explanation.surface: An order to give a gift that covers the setter's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to rule over or control.

clue.text: Measures ricochets blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the first letter

parts.note: a ricochet bounces off a surface

explanation.surface: Rebounding bullets that blow off the top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounces are units of weight, so measures in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Beneath going after small part

indicators.note: going after puts this word after the other letter

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
under means below

explanation.surface: Something below is chasing a small fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunder is to part or split apart, a literary verb.

clue.text: Sweated beginning to take exercise

indicators.note: to take means the first word holds the other

parts.note: a seed is the beginning or germ of something
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Someone sweated at the start of a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeped means oozed out slowly, as sweat leaks from skin.

clue.text: Bug with a giant nose twitching

indicators.note: twitching describes jerky movement, so the letters jump around

explanation.surface: An insect with a huge, twitching snout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect but is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or provoke them.

clue.text: Pose in front of beach and sunbathe

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of beach

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: Strike a pose on the beach and soak up the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here places ASK after the front letter of beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask is to lie in warmth and sunshine.

clue.text: Hits ball and takes serve initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A tennis or cricket player strikes the ball and serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are strikes, as when a player hits with a bat.

clue.text: Boot that is following fit

indicators.note: following puts the abbreviation after the other word

parts.note: fit means healthy, well
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boot that fits properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is a wellington, a rubber waterproof boot, in British usage.

clue.text: Innuendo perhaps is never too outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous signals the letters are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: Suggestive remarks are never too shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is one kind of implied hidden suggestion, an example of a subtext.
